description:
🚀 SpectraX is a team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 working on Planet X and SPHEREx.

We're building an interactive platform that helps people explore SPHEREx infrared sky data and discover the hidden universe. Our goal is to make complex space data accessible to scientists, students, and the public through engaging visualizations and tools.
summary:
PROJECT SPECTRA X is an automated data analysis and visualization platform built to search for Planet X using near-infrared sky survey data from NASA's SPHEREx mission.
To address the challenge of finding faint, distant objects hidden in massive astronomical datasets, our team developed a pipeline that filters out background stars, galaxies, and cosmic noise across SPHEREx’s 102 spectral bands. By analyzing thermal infrared signatures alongside six-month parallax shifts, the tool isolates slow-moving, icy candidates in the outer solar system and displays them on an interactive dashboard for easy inspection.
This project is important because manually sifting through terabytes of multi-wavelength sky data is nearly impossible for human researchers alone. PROJECT SPECTRA X accelerates the discovery of trans-Neptunian objects, reduces false positives, and creates a scalable, accessible tool that helps both astronomers and citizen scientists map the uncharted edges of our solar system.
details:
Project Overview: What It Does & How It Works

PROJECT SPECTRA X is an automated data analysis and visualization tool designed to search for Planet X (Planet Nine) using spectral data from NASA's SPHEREx mission.

  • Data Processing: Our system ingests all-sky near-infrared survey data across SPHEREx's 102 spectral bands.
  • Anomaly Detection: It filters out known stars, galaxies, and background cosmic noise to isolate faint, cold, slow-moving objects in the outer solar system.
  • Orbit Tracking: By comparing sky maps captured every six months, the tool tracks parallax shifts and proper motion to flag potential Planet X candidates.

Key Benefits

  • Handles Massive Datasets: Automates the review of terabytes of multi-band infrared data that would take astronomers years to inspect manually.
  • Improves Detection Accuracy: Combines multi-wavelength thermal signatures with orbital motion tracking to reduce false positives from distant background galaxies.
  • Open & Accessible: Provides an intuitive dashboard so both researchers and citizen scientists can inspect flagged candidates and spectral light curves.

Intended Impact

  • Advancing Planetary Science: Accelerates the search for undiscovered trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) and helps confirm or rule out the existence of Planet X.
  • Reusable Framework: Our detection pipeline can be adapted to spot other faint, cold celestial bodies, such as brown dwarfs or rogue planets, in future sky surveys.

Tools, Languages, & Software Used

  • Programming Languages: Python (for data processing, machine learning, and astronomical calculations), JavaScript/HTML/CSS (for the interactive web interface).
  • Astronomy & Data Libraries: Astropy, NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, and Scikit-learn / TensorFlow (adjust based on what you used).
  • Data Sources & Software: NASA SPHEREx simulated/mission datasets, IPAC/IRSA archives, GitHub for version control, and [insert any visualization or UI tools like React, Plotly, or Figma].

Creativity & Innovation

  • Spectral Fingerprinting: Instead of relying solely on visible light movement, we treat SPHEREx's 102 infrared bands as a unique "thermal barcode" to separate icy outer-solar-system bodies from warmer background stars.
  • Interactive Sky Explorer: We paired complex astrophysical filtering with a clean, visual interface that lets users toggle between different infrared wavelengths to "see" hidden anomalies.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Faint Signal-to-Noise Ratio: Because Planet X is extremely distant and cold, its reflected sunlight and thermal emission are very weak; we prioritized noise-reduction algorithms to preserve faint signals.
  • Orbital Mechanics & Parallax: We accounted for Earth's own orbital motion around the Sun across six-month survey intervals to accurately separate nearby solar system objects from stationary background stars.
  • Scalability & Speed: We optimized our code to process large sky patches efficiently without requiring supercomputing resources.
